findings.what: Two independent full runs of this spec on the review rig each produced 2-3 failures (net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED / 30s locator timeouts) in DIFFERENT, pre-existing tests each time (#736 zoom/nav tests, #732 /pending test, 'Escape closes the overlay rail', 'rail is DOCKED at 1280') — none of them tests #625 touched. Every #625-owned cell (members-invite-walk.spec.ts x3, the new 'invite-acceptance card reflows' test, and the two narrow-face-loop/reflow additions inside pre-existing tests) passed cleanly in both runs.
findings.evidence: Run 1 (combined members-invite-walk + responsive-shell-walk, 28 tests): 25 passed, 3 failed at spec.ts:755/789/830, all net::ERR_ABORTED/ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED against the Next dev server (cascading, consistent with the server itself going unresponsive rather than 3 independent assertion failures). Run 2 (responsive-shell-walk alone, 25 tests): 23 passed, 2 different failures at spec.ts:344 (30000ms locator.fill timeout) and :367 (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED). git diff origin/main...HEAD confirms neither failing test in either run is inside #625's diff hunks (@@ -134,+42 and @@ -622,+11 only). Confirmed via `git rev-parse` that this worktree is exactly the reviewed HEAD (c6f18f8c), so this is not stale state.
findings.fix: No action against this branch: the failures are non-deterministic across reruns, land on tests this diff never touched, and every #625-owned Playwright cell (members-invite-walk x3, the new narrow/reflow cells) passed in every run observed. Most likely local/CI resource contention under a long linear 1-worker Chromium suite on this Windows rig (the ticket's own brief already lists known Windows-specific Playwright reds — #707, #693, thread-live-clarify — as pre-existing and not to be 'fixed' by this ticket). Recording this only so a future reviewer isn't surprised by a non-repro red on this same file; not a reason to hold the ticket.

findings.what: The brief's binding instruction (brief-625.md line 66) says to declare caller_context/firm_members_visible/firm_invites_visible in the existing SHARED_RPC_VERBS map. The worker instead added a new, parallel CORE_RELATION_HANDOVERS census/test. Verified this is a sound, disclosed substitution rather than a silent narrowing: SHARED_RPC_VERBS's own census regex (RPC_VERB_OPENER, :937) matches only `verb === "x"` / `fn === "x"` / `path === "/rest/v1/rpc/x"` shapes and requires >=2 lane-mock claimants; the three relations here are queried as plain PostgREST relation reads (`path === "/rest/v1/caller_context"`, no `/rpc/`) answered by exactly one lane mock plus serve-built.mjs's own CORE — so literally declaring them in SHARED_RPC_VERBS would make the existing verb-ownership test's own self-check (`assert.ok(actual.length > 1, ...)`) fail, since the census would find zero or one claimant, never a collision. The new CORE-handover test was run and passes (16/16 in e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, including the new census) and functionally polices the exact same class of defect (an undeclared handover of a CORE-answered read) the brief was asking for.
findings.evidence: Read RPC_VERB_OPENER regex and rpcVerbCensus() at e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts:937-949; confirmed lib/firm/caller-context.ts:50 and lib/members/reads.ts:91-92 name these three as RELATIONs, not RPC verbs. Ran `node --import ./test/bootstrap.mjs --import tsx --test e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts` on the worktree: 16/16 pass including 'CORE-handover census · the member reads taken over from serve-built.mjs stay DECLARED...'. Worker's own report names this exact reasoning under 'Assumptions (orchestrator review) #1'.
findings.fix: No change needed — flagging only so the reviewer-of-record explicitly signs off on this documented deviation from the brief's literal text (the brief's premise that these three reads are 'RPC verbs' was itself imprecise; they are relation reads). If a stricter reading is wanted, the brief itself should be corrected in a follow-up rather than the code forced into a census mechanism that cannot express the fact being declared.
